# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This resource has been developed to support Year 11 students preparing for
**NCEA Level 1 Achievement Standard 91946**: *Interpret and apply mathematical
and statistical information in context* (4 credits).

## What this standard is about

In this standard you will learn to:

- **Read and interpret** statistical displays, tables, and graphs
- **Apply** mathematical and statistical ideas to real-world problems
- **Communicate** findings clearly using statistical language
- **Evaluate** statistical claims made in media and everyday life

## How to use this book

Each chapter builds on the previous one. You will find:

- Clear explanations of key concepts with New Zealand examples
- Interactive R code blocks showing how statistics is done with real data
- Practice questions at Achievement, Merit, and Excellence levels
- Glossary boxes highlighting important vocabulary

::: {.callout-tip}
## Achievement Standard at a Glance

| Grade | What you need to do |
|-------|---------------------|
| **Achieved** | Interpret and apply statistical information |
| **Merit** | Interpret and apply statistical information with justification |
| **Excellence** | Interpret and apply statistical information with statistical insight |
:::

## Tools we use

All data visualisations and calculations in this book are produced using **R** and
rendered with **Quarto**. You do not need to be able to write R code to succeed
in this standard — the code blocks are provided so your teacher can demonstrate
concepts live and so you can explore data yourself if you choose.

```{r}
#| label: welcome-plot
#| fig-cap: "An example of the kind of visualisations we will create in this book."
#| echo: false

# A motivating example: NZ weather data (simulated for illustration)
set.seed(42)
months <- factor(month.abb, levels = month.abb)
avg_temp <- c(17, 17, 15, 12, 9, 7, 6, 8, 10, 13, 14, 16)

barplot(
  avg_temp,
  names.arg = months,
  col = "#2c7bb6",
  border = "white",
  main = "Average Monthly Temperature — Wellington, NZ (°C)",
  ylab = "Temperature (°C)",
  xlab = "Month",
  las = 1
)
abline(h = mean(avg_temp), col = "#d7191c", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topright", legend = paste0("Mean = ", round(mean(avg_temp), 1), "°C"),
       col = "#d7191c", lwd = 2, lty = 2, bty = "n")
```
